Sewadjkare III: Egypt's 14th Dynasty Pharaoh

Avaris, Eastern Nile Delta (c. 1700 BC): The enigmatic pharaoh of the 14th Dynasty, Sewadjkare III, left an indelible mark on ancient Egypt's Second Intermediate Period. His reign, though shrouded in mystery, was marked by a complex interplay of power struggles, cultural exchange, and the emergence of new artistic and architectural styles.

As a king of the 14th Dynasty, Sewadjkare III would have reigned from Avaris over the eastern Nile Delta and possibly over the western Delta as well.

The specifics of his life, however, remain elusive, with historical records offering only fragmented glimpses into his rule.

Despite the scarcity of information, Sewadjkare III's significance in the broader context of ancient Egyptian history is undeniable.
